prompt: Write the join so every partition is kept even when no group has committed to it: a LEFT JOIN of `commits` (alias c) onto `partitions` (alias p), matching on both topic and partition_id with AND. The partitions table is on the left.
template:
-- EXPECTED: [["audit", 0, 10], ["empty", 0, 0], ["orders", 0, 100], ["orders", 1, 210], ["payments", 0, 40]]

-- Tables are loaded for you: partitions(topic, partition_id, log_end_offset) and commits(group_id, topic, partition_id, committed_offset).
SELECT p.topic, p.partition_id,
       COALESCE(MAX(c.committed_offset), 0) AS best
FROM partitions p
@@BLANK@@
GROUP BY p.topic, p.partition_id
ORDER BY p.topic, p.partition_id;
answer: LEFT JOIN commits c ON c.topic = p.topic AND c.partition_id = p.partition_id
why: LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table (partitions) even with no match, filling the commit columns with NULL.
